UI_trait_DanDependentdesc:
You cannot go long without a drink.

After 24 hours without any intoxication you start craving: stress climbs by about 0.06 per hour.
After 48 hours dry the shakes turn painful: pain rises by about 3 per hour on top of the stress.
Any drink that gets you even slightly intoxicated resets the clock and ends the withdrawal.
UI_trait_DanBrittledesc:
Your bones give out easily.

Any hit that deals 2 or more damage has a 20% chance to fracture a random forearm, hand or lower leg.
The fracture is a serious one (severity 40 to 80) and must be splinted like any other.
Only one fracture per limb at a time.
UI_trait_DanFumblerdesc:
Your grip is unreliable.

Every weapon swing has a 1% chance to throw the weapon out of your hands when you are calm, unhurt and rested. Panic adds up to 6%, pain up to 6% and fatigue up to 5%, so a terrified, wounded, exhausted swing fails about one time in six.
The weapon lands on the ground at your feet and has to be picked up again.
UI_trait_DanJinxeddesc:
Luck is not on your side.

When a container generates its loot for the first time near you, there is a 35% chance one random item from it is simply gone.
Containers that were already looted or generated before are unaffected.
UI_trait_DanSpiralingdesc:
Your mood is not something you control.

Pain and stress drag it down all the time: at full pain you lose a point of happiness a minute.
Depressive episodes start at random, about once a week in a calm life and more often when you are stressed, hurting, exhausted or shut indoors. They last from one to six days and hold your unhappiness up to a floor set by how bad the episode is. Books, magazines, TV and radio lift you for a few minutes and then it comes back.
What helps: a drink (it lifts the floor while you are drunk, and quietly deepens the episode), a cigarette (a couple of hours), a comforting meal (a few hours), keeping up regular exercise, and hours spent outdoors. Exercise and time outside also shorten the episode.
Antidepressants do not give you the usual instant lift. Taken one a day, without gaps, they build up over about two weeks: episodes become rarer, shallower and shorter, and pain and stress bite a little less. The first few days on them make you queasy and tired. Stop after a week or more on them and you get a few rough days. A bottle is about ten days.
UI_trait_DanBadDaydesc:
Everything that could go wrong this morning did.

You start blind drunk (intoxication 100), with a nasty cold (strength 50, coughing from the first minute) and a deep shard of glass buried in your groin.
You were in the shower: no clothes, and soaked to the bone.
If you start indoors, a random room of the house (never the kitchen or garage) is already on fire.
Applied once, to a new character only. Profession and other traits are unaffected.
UI_trait_DanSchizophreniadesc:
Your mind plays tricks on you.

Every 10 minutes there is a chance of an episode: a zombie sprinting straight at you that fades away before it reaches you, a zombie groan or scratch from somewhere nearby that is not there, a door or window near you thumping as if something is on the other side, a whisper from just behind you or muttering through the wall, glass breaking somewhere close, footsteps that go nowhere, or a sudden bout of panic.
Base chance is 12% per 10 minutes and never drops below that, even when you are doing everything right: about one episode every 80 minutes.
Stress adds up to 30%, unhappiness up to 20%, tiredness up to 20%, and night adds 8%. At the worst, expect one nearly every 10 minutes.
Phantom sounds and thumps add a little panic. Panic bouts add a lot.
Nothing happens while you sleep.
UI_trait_DanAsthmadesc:
Your airways are a pressure gauge, not a stat penalty. Cannot be taken with the vanilla Asthmatic trait.

Airway irritation builds from cold air (below 10 C), decaying corpses within 3 tiles, exertion (endurance under 40%), running or sprinting, and panic (a racing heart and fast, shallow breathing; the worse the panic, the faster it builds, and no mask helps with that one). It drains away only slowly, when you rest in clean, warm air: about four hours from an attack back to clear. Sleep clears it twice as fast, if you can sleep.
A dust or surgical mask halves the cold and corpse build-up. A gas mask blocks it entirely and cuts exertion build-up by 80%.
Irritation 25%: warning only. 50%: endurance recovers at half speed and you cough now and then (zombies within 6 tiles hear it). 75%: endurance stops recovering, you cough often (10 tiles), and you cannot sleep: you wake up gasping.
90%: asthma attack. Endurance drains to nothing, you cough constantly (30 tiles), your health drops to a floor of 15%, and every minute of it piles on panic, which feeds the attack. It ends only when irritation falls back under 75%, and it will not do that on its own.
A rescue inhaler (10 puffs) knocks irritation down by half and sets your heart racing. Use it mid-attack and you are back to wheezing, not cured. You start with one; more turn up in bathroom cabinets and medical loot, and rarely in pockets and bags.
UI_trait_DanGlutendesc:
Wheat makes you ill. Bread, bagels, pasta, noodles, cereal, crackers, cookies, cake, pie, dough, pancakes, waffles, sandwiches, burgers, pizza, pastries, tortillas, dumplings and beer all count. Rice, potatoes, corn, oats, fruit, meat and vegetables are safe.

About twenty minutes after eating wheat the reaction starts and builds over half an hour. How bad it gets depends on how much you ate: a slice of bread is a rough few hours, a whole loaf or a bowl of pasta is a full flare.
A flare brings stomach cramps (pain), nausea (the Queasy moodle, climbing to Nauseous), low mood and creeping stress. They are held up for as long as the flare lasts: painkillers ease the cramps for a while, then they come back.
A full flare takes about ten hours of rest to clear, less if you sleep it off. Eating more wheat on top of it stacks.
UI_trait_DanVegetariandesc:
You do not eat animals. Meat, poultry, fish, seafood, insects, pet food and anything cooked with them are off the menu: the Eat option is greyed out and you will not go through with it. Eggs and dairy are fine.

Hunting, trapping and fishing feed everyone but you. Plan around cans, crops, foraging, eggs and milk, and read the ingredients on a stew before you count on it.
UI_trait_DanDiabetes1desc:
Your body makes no insulin. Cannot be taken with Type 2.

Blood sugar is tracked in the background (normal is 70 to 180). Carbohydrates in what you eat and drink push it up: sugar, candy, soda, juice and fruit hit inside half an hour, bread, pasta and potatoes over two hours. With nothing to bring it down it also creeps up about 10 an hour on its own, and panic pushes it up. Running, hard exertion and sleep pull it down a little. Alcohol pulls it down for as long as you are drunk, and hides the warning signs while it does.
Only injected insulin brings it down properly: one dose lowers it by about 50 over four hours, starting after fifteen minutes. A loaf of bread is worth about 400, a can of cola about 125. Too much insulin, or insulin without a meal, sends you low.
Low (under 70): shaky hands that drop weapons, rising panic. Under 55: endurance and mood drain too. Under 40: health drains to a floor of 15%.
High (over 180): thirst and tiredness. Over 250: queasy and low. Over 350: health drains to 15%, and after a full day up there the floor is gone.
The warning signs are vague and overlap. A glucose meter and test strips give the number. You start with a meter, 25 strips and three pens of 40 doses each; more turn up in medical loot, pharmacies and fridges.
UI_trait_DanDiabetes2desc:
Your body still makes insulin, but it does not listen to it as well as it should. Cannot be taken with Type 1.

Blood sugar works as for Type 1 (see that trait), except that your own insulin pulls it back toward a resting level on its own. How well depends on insulin resistance, which is set by your body weight: none at 75 kg or under, full at 110 kg or over. At full resistance sugar rests around 220 and a meal takes many hours to clear; at none it rests around 100 and clears in an hour or two. Regular exercise cuts resistance by up to a quarter, and a metformin pill a day cuts it by a third more. Lose the weight and the condition is, for practical purposes, gone.
Injected insulin works for you too, at reduced strength, and can send you low just the same.
The warning signs are the same vague ones. You start with a meter, 25 strips and a bottle of metformin (10 pills).
UI_trait_DanRenFairedesc:
Every summer, the garb, the turkey legs, the sparring ring and a booth at the smithy. It turns out to have been training.

+1 Spear, +1 Long Blade, +1 Axe and +1 Blacksmithing, with the faster experience gain that comes with a starting level in each.
UI_trait_DanGymRegulardesc:
Three mornings a week, without fail, right up until the end of the world.

Every exercise starts at half regularity (50 of 100) instead of none, the same head start a Fitness Instructor gets. That is the bar in the fitness window: reps come easier and stiffen you less, and your Vitality exercise score starts at neutral rather than empty, which also counts toward Type 2 insulin resistance and easing depressive episodes from day one.
It fades like any regularity does: keep training or lose it. Applied once, to a new character.
